question: Ali's back pain is the worst it has ever been. He starts a herbal cream that day; two weeks later he is far better. Why?
options: The pain would have eased anyway
answer: The pain would have eased anyway. People start treatments when pain peaks, and new back pain usually improves fast: in pooled cohort studies, pain fell by more than half within the first month. Whatever is begun on the worst day rides that slope down and collects the credit.
move: Anything started at the worst moment will look like it worked.
ask: What remedy do I swear by that I only ever tried on my very worst days?
trap: The cream eased the pain, since relief followed the very day he began.
reference: Pengel et al., Acute low back pain: systematic review of its prognosis, BMJ, 2003
